mechanism_narrative: Sustained recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT from their four-week lows signals a return of commuting and routine out-of-home movement that mechanically lifts weekday and weekend retail footfall over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -26.3 to -16.4 and TRANSIT rose from -51.3 to -42.0 across four weekly means
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is less than or equal to its mean over the last 28 days while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continue to rise.

mechanism_narrative: A steady decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility from +9.6 to +5.9 means fewer people are staying home during the day, which raises exposure to retail-and-recreation venues and lifts RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from +9.6 to +5.9 over the four weekly means
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL continues its decline but mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES recovers above -18 while PARKS simultaneously holds above -10, the metro exhibits a broad return of routine and leisure outings; this interaction amplifies discretionary retail visits and raises RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES above -18.0 and PARKS above -10.0 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved to -16.4 while PARKS was -7.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: In weeks when WORKPLACES is above -18.0 and PARKS is above -10.0, mean RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks fails to exceed its prior two-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: A crossing of TRANSIT above -45.0 marks a discrete relaxation in mobility constraints; commuter and discretionary trips then follow with a short lag, lifting RETAIL_REC in the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT reached -42.0 at t-0w after -51.3 at t-3w
failure_condition: After TRANSIT first exceeds -45.0, mean RETAIL_REC over the following 7 days is lower than the mean over the 7 days before the crossing.

mechanism_narrative: Late-February seasonal normalization after the holiday and Omicron-depressed January lifts baseline retail-and-recreation activity; the four-week RETAIL_REC trajectory should continue upward through early March.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose from -16.3 to -11.6 across the four weekly means
failure_condition: The next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not higher than the last 28-day mean, contradicting the seasonal rebound.

mechanism_narrative: Falling RESIDENTIAL below +6.0 combined with rising TRANSIT above -45.0 indicates that people are substituting home time for transit-linked outings; this interaction increases retail-and-recreation trips over two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below +6.0 while TRANSIT is above -45.0
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell to +5.9 and TRANSIT rose to -42.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: When RESIDENTIAL is below +6.0 and TRANSIT is above -45.0, the following two-week mean of RETAIL_REC does not exceed the preceding two-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent above-baseline GROCERY_PHARM mobility above +2.0 signals continued health-cautious necessity-only shopping; this behavior diverts trips from discretionary retail and keeps RETAIL_REC depressed over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stays above +2.0 for two consecutive weekly means
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM remained positive at +3.3, +1.7, +3.4, +2.7 across the four weekly means
failure_condition: While GROCERY_PHARM remains above +2.0 for two consecutive weeks, mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: Under a formal reopening regime, continued WORKPLACES and TRANSIT recovery translates into higher discretionary mobility because policy no longer suppresses capacity; RETAIL_REC should rise over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES improves for two consecutive weeks under an active reopening regime
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improved over the four weekly means
failure_condition: In the reopening regime, mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to its mean over the last 28 days despite continued WORKPLACES improvement.
